en: The *Pratisarā-stotra*: Om, homage to the illustrious Pratisarā!
O Pratisarā, I bow to you, who are worshipped by the hosts of immortals.
[She is] the one who provides protection at all times for those practicing the path;
she grants excellent protection against the suffering of falling into chasms, fire, or the ocean;
she destroys the fear of enemies and poison; and she bestows sovereignty, enjoyments, and other blessings. (1)

To those who have surrounded themselves with their own kin, who have been granted liberation by the faithful, who have gathered a multitude of sins, for whom the attainment of liberation is the sole path,
who have brought forth the creation of men and gods, and who have caused the destruction of the bodiless god of love;
To the sages Garga and others who offer praise, who are solely intent on the protection of all; || 2 ||

I always pay homage to you, who have struck down all obstacles, who are uniquely honored by the entire world, who are blessed by the Ten Powers, who are most excellent among the five goddesses, and who are a refuge for those in difficult circumstances.
Like a forest that has been consumed by a wildfire and has become desolate. || 3 ||
She who fulfills the noble desires of all people like a wish-granting cow (kāmadhenu), who is the supreme creeper of the desire-yielding tree (kalpavṛkṣa) for the attainment of cherished fruits,
and whose pair of lotus-feet are worshipped by asuras, gods, humans, and others—
Upon her chest, she is adorned with various beautiful garlands of jewels and other ornaments. || 4 ||
Resplendent as a hundred moons, white as a conch shell or a kunda flower,
with the fears of the planets entirely pacified, she whose essence is Vajrasattva,
wearing earrings that sway gracefully upon her ears—
I bow to her who is illuminated by the crest-jewels atop their crowns. || 5 ||
O Mother, you who deliver one from all suffering, be gracious; quickly protect me and my mother, whose protection has now vanished.
May I, who have wept with compassion, be established in the well-being of your mercy.
You have cast us into a lake of suffering; you are our refuge, you are our refuge.
Whoever always recites this hymn of the *Pratisarā* shall have fire, water, poison, thieves, tigers, and diseases—
those causes of death and fear— destroyed by her.
He attained a firmness of mind that was not broken at every step by desire.
Attended by her own people, increasing virtue, desire, and wealth, and liberated from hosts of enemies, she enjoys nothing but happiness;
always a granter of desires, she bestows vast enjoyments.
Having had all their sins destroyed, they attain liberation at the end.
With tears streaming from his eyes and palms joined in reverence, he lamented and offered this hymn of praise to the Mother of the Three Worlds:
"May all prosperity come to me through the fire of my every being."
Thus, with such a well-disposed mind, the protection of one's own virtue is easily accomplished. || 9 ||
May all the karma to be experienced by those like me— who have harmed their brothers and mothers— ripen upon me alone, even for the sake of the hosts of gods and men;
exert, exert yourselves with fortitude, so that liberation may be easily attained.
May there never be sin dwelling within the abode of the belly.
At that time, those whose minds are constantly pure and virtuous shall attain enlightenment after dwelling in the great hells;
for by providing protection to the world, they shall achieve the state of absolute liberation.
Thus, with a mind full of joy and a heart smeared by his own deed, he remained. || 11 ||
Saying, "O Pratisarā, bring Sāmbikā down;
do not delay for even a moment," he stood there as a child, his body smeared with terrifying poison, censuring his own deed.
For he repeatedly remembered here that refuge which provides protection for all.
Oh, how truly blessed is the sole Mother of the World, whose destiny has been fulfilled and who is free from fear of the hosts of enemies!
By her power, fire—though produced from a most sinful source—is rendered as cool as water. (13)
Oh, how great is her power!
For by the mere remembrance of her, even fire, water, mountains, and dry land become as if filled with wonder.
Vaiśvānara attained that twofold form.
The body of Gopā, cooled by its fall into the lake, was as if excessively warm for the sake of not perishing;
it was cast from a very great distance by a most wicked person, yet providentially delivered to a noble family on all sides.
The *Pratisarā-stotra*, extracted from the *Śrī-bhadrakalpāvadāna* and composed by the child while still in the womb of Yaśodharā, is complete.
